title: Cross-Agent State Channel Pollution

invariant.statement: When two or more agents share a state channel (vector DB, KV store, message queue, filesystem), reads from the channel must include cryptographic provenance binding the value to the writing agent and the user-session under whose authority it was written. Reads without provenance MUST be treated as untrusted input.

claim.statement: If agent A and agent B share a state channel C, and B reads from C without verifying the provenance of each value, then any user who can prompt A to write attacker-controlled content into C can later prompt B to read that content as authoritative state. The attack succeeds even when A and B serve different users, different tenants, or different privilege levels — because C is the actual trust boundary, not the agent identities. This is shared-channel injection, the multi-agent generalization of stored XSS.

mitigation.summary: Every shared-channel write records {writer_agent_id, session_id, signed_at, signature_over(value)}. Every read returns the value PLUS the provenance record. Consumers MUST verify the signature, MUST check that writer_agent_id is on the consumer's allowlist of trusted writers for that namespace, AND MUST scope the read to the session/tenant the consumer is currently serving. A shared channel without provenance is a stored-injection sink.

references: OWASP LLM02: Insecure Output Handling (cross-context variant)
Stored XSS pattern — multi-agent generalization (Hardy/Madnick analogue, 2024)
